notes.taste: Deep ruby red in colour with violet tinged reflections. Ripe plums, blackberry jam and cocoa on the nose. Firm and well balanced on the palate with soft tannins and supporting acidity. A long lingering finish of fruit and spices.
notes.food: Passo Doble is a versatile wine which goes well with grilled or roast red meats, chickpea based dishes, aubergine hamburgers, or strong-flavoured cheeses. Serve at 18°C in large wine glasses.
notes.made: The technique used here is Masi’s speciality: double fermentation. After soft pressing of the Malbec grapes, on-skin fermentation lasted 15 days in stainless steel tanks at a constant 21-23°C. The second fermentation was induced with selected yeasts and used 15% of whole Corvina grapes given a brief appassimento treatment before pressing. This fermentation lasted 15 days at 18-20°C and was followed by a malolactic fermentation. It was further matured 9 months in French oak casks (70% second usage, 30% new). Followed by at least two weeks of bottle age.
notes.vines: Organically cultivated vineyards located in the famous wine-producing area of Mendoza, in the western part of Argentina which lies at an altitude of 950-1050 metres above-sea-level in the Tupungato valley. The ground is stony, sandy and chalky. Low organic substance and good mineral content throughout.

notes.taste: Pale yellow with bright green highlights. The nose is fresh and inviting: green apple and fresh pear with fine mineral support. Screech

notes.taste: Amber colour; dense nose of spice, brown sugar, vanilla, white chocolate and caramel; rich, toffee flavour with a hint of brine and a spicy finish. A smooth and balanced blend.
notes.food: Enjoy it in a Dark N' Stormy or any other dark rum cocktails.
notes.made: Rum is a distilled alcoholic spirit made by fermenting then distilling sugarcane molasses or sugarcane juice. The distillate, a clear liquid, is usually aged in oak barrels. Long before any Canadian liquor board was created, the Jamaican rum that was eventually to be known as Screech was a mainstay of the traditional Newfoundland diet.
notes.vines: Imported from Jamaica for over 200 years. At that time in history, salt fish was being shipped to the West Indies in exchange for rum. This resulted in fish becoming the national dish for Jamaicans and rum becoming the traditional drink for Newfoundlanders. As the story goes, a visiting American WWII serviceman downed the rum in one quick toss. His howls of distress caused a bystander to rush to his aid, roaring “What the cripes was that ungodly screech?” The taciturn Newf simply replied, “The screech?” ‘Tis the rum, me son.” As word of the incident spread more soldiers began trying this mysterious rum, adopting it as their favorite. Thus a legend was born.

items.house: A true part of Newfoundland’s tradition. Screech Rum has been imported from Jamaica for over 200 years. In the early days, they were not overly concerned with alcohol content. This product use to be bottled unlabeled but as the story goes, a visiting American World War II serviceman downed the rum in one quick shot. His screams of distress brought the attention of bystanders who heard him howl, “What the cripes was that ungodly Screech?!”

notes.made: 80 % is hand picked and 20 % is through mechanical picking. 4 to 12 months aged in stainless steel tanks. Grapes are sourced from multi-climatic situated vineyards: coastal, southern and mountain estates add to the complexity of the wine.

Richer, more full-bodied and expansive in the mouth, offering soft pear, honey, salted toffee and subtle spice. Good structure.”

notes.food: Enjoy this wine with grilled steak, BBQ, smoked ham and other full-flavored dishes.

notes.food: Delicious on its own or enjoy with shellfish, seafood, white meat, mixed salads or goat cheese.
notes.made: Each grape variety (Grenache blanc, Bourboulenc, Roussanne) was vinified individually to develop its own characteristics. To boost aromatic potential, fermentation was done at low temperature (12-14°C / 54-58°F). The ageing in vats lasted for 6 months before bottling. This wine is Vegan (no animal-derived products were used to clarify or in fining the wine).
notes.vines: The Cotes du Rhone is one of the largest and most diverse French appellation with more than 35,000 Ha (86,000 acres) from south of Lyon all the way to Avignon. Along the length of the Rhône River, the Côtes du Rhône vineyards thrive on rich and varied terroirs. Its history starts in 125 BC when the Romans first planted vines in the region. In 1650, regulations were introduced to ensure that the wine was genuine and to guarantee its quality. A royal decree in 1737 stated that all barrels destined for sale or transport must be branded with the letters “C.D.R”. Finally, the region was awarded the ‘AOC’ (Registered Designation of Origin) Côtes du Rhône in 1937.

items.name: Brut Nature

notes.taste: Yellow in colour with glints of light amber. The nose has an intense bouquet combining sweet flowers yellow fruits and lightly roasted dried nuts . It evolves towards spicy and citrus notes with a hint of pepper.
notes.food: Fantastic with fatty smoked fish (tuna, salmon) as well as cured hams and also with hard cheeses.
notes.made: The grapes are grown exclusively in the Côteaux de Cumières in Louis Roederer's bio-dynamic estate . Brut Nature is made in the Traditional Method, aged for 5 years in cellar and left for a minimum of 6 months after disgorging to attain the perfect maturity. No dosage. Two thirds of the cuvee is Pinot Noir and Pinot Meunier and the remaining one-third is Chardonnay. 25 % is vinified in oak casks with no malolactic fermentation.
notes.vines: From the bio-dynamic estate in Côteaux de Cumières. There are distinct variations in climate. The majority of its vineyards are situated in a temperate maritime climate with slight continental influences, particularly in the south-east.

items.name: Brut Nature Rosé

notes.taste: Cumières clay hillside, turned towards the sun and basking in its light, is a hallowed enclave, whose grapes always possess a remarkable fragrance and richness. These black soils, on the banks of the Marne river, have long been known to produce generous, opulent and intensely fragrant grapes. In warmer years the grapes obtain incredible ripeness and a higher vibration which gives us this lovely contrast between fruity intensity and salinity.
notes.made: Conceived as an exchange and shaped by friendship, this wine is first and foremost a result of the free-thinking that came out of a meeting between Louis Roederer CEO Frédéric Rouzaud, his cellar master Jean-Baptiste Lécaillon and the designer Philippe Starck. Their conversations led to the creation of the very first Brut Nature in 2006 and the relationship continued to grow over the years. 50% Pinot Noir 37% Chardonnay 13% Meunier. Dosage 0 g/L
notes.vines: The Brut Nature was born from an idea of the dreamed-for, perfect champagne. It is a wine that captures the freshness of the clay soils in a sunny year, a wine of truth, the testimony to an encounter, a soil, a year, free spirits and the independent spirit that runs through the Champagne House. It is a champagne that perfectly encapsulates this new exploration of a Louis Roederer terroir.

items.name: Brut Vintage

notes.taste: Golden yellow with soft amber tints and a bright, gentle sparkle. The subtle bouquet reveals spring-like notes of fresh citrus fruits, smoky mineral aromas and hints of lightly toasted almonds. The wine has a talc-like chalkiness and is both soft and full bodied, with a silky long finish.
notes.food: Ideal as an aperitif, due to its freshness and finesse, Its structure makes it a splendid accompaniment to fine cuisine which pairs beautifully with lobster, shellfish, white fish and white meats.
notes.made: The blend is 70% Pinot Noir and 30% Chardonnay, with 20% of the wine vinified in oak tuns with weekly bâtonnage (stirring by hand); it is not subjected to malolactic fermentation. The Vintage cuvée is aged, on average, for four years in Louis Roederer’s cellars and left for six months after dégorgement (disgorging) to attain optimal maturity. The dosage is 9 g/l.
notes.vines: This Vintage Cuvée uses the two blended wines from two seperate regions. 70% cool-climate Pinot Noir from Verzy and Verzenay (Montagne de Reims) and 30% Chardonnay from a very warm, south/southwest-facing vineyard in Chouilly (Côte des Blancs).

items.name: Collection Brut

notes.taste: Delicate and elegant. Its reserve wines bring rich round flavors that make it vibrant, fresh and generous. From the outset, Brut Premier affirms its personality and seduction: the texture is full and generous and, in a fairly unexpected way, integrates characteristics of maturity associated with fruitier and more refreshing notes. The wine has a fresh festive finesse. In the mouth, the wine has structure, richness and length. It is a full, complex wine that is both modern and powerful, while remaining a great classic.
notes.food: Collection Brut can be served for many occasions. It is ideal as an aperitif due to its freshness and finesse. The structure also makes it a splendid accompaniment to fine cuisine. This lovely Champagne pairs beautifully with lobster or shellfish, honey and brioche, liver and white fruit (peaches and plums), as well as Terrine of foie gras with almond jelly.
notes.made: Driven by a new ambition and freedom, with the creation of Collection, we are writing the next chapter of our story. The times we live in; climate change and the importance of practising a sustainable viticulture that respects the living environment in order to fully express the qualities of the terroir, these are all factors that must be taken into account. Collection Brut is an evolution in structure, form and style.
notes.vines: The grapes are harvested from 40 of the best and most diverse different vineyard plots from within Montagne de Reims and Cote de Blancs in the Champagne region. The grapes for Collection Brut are 40% Pinot Noir, 40% Chardonnay and 20% Pinot Meunier. Collection Brut also features a big increase in the presence of reserve wines in the final blend over its predecessor, Brut Premier.

items.name: Cristal

notes.taste: Amber hue with green and orange tints. Fine, even and lively effervescence. A complex and intense bouquet disclosing candied citrus, yellow fruit, pear, pollen and toasted almonds. The delicately seductive bouquet shows depth with a well-honed precision.
notes.food: Not just a celebration wine. This remarkable Champagne is perfect with white fish and white meats.
notes.made: Produced only in the best years, Cristal is composed of Grand Crus selected grapes from the Montagne de Reims, the Marne Valley and the Côte des Blancs. 60 % is of Chardonnay and 40 % from Pinot Noir is made in the classic Traditional Method. 20 % is vinified in oak casks and 20 % goes through Malolactic Fermentation. The wine is generally aged for 6 years, sometimes longer, in cellars and left for a minimum of 8 months after disgorging. Originally created in 1876 to satisfy the demanding tastes of Tsar Alexander II Russia. The emperor asked Louis Roederer to reserve the House’s best cuvée for him every year. He was particularly fond of the House’s wine. To distinguish this cuvée, this exceptional champagne came in a flat-bottomed, transparent lead-crystal bottle. The new brand was named after this precious material, 'Cristal', which is particularly transparent and luminous.
notes.vines: Harvested from the famous Grand Crus selected sites of the Montagne de Reims, the Marne Valley and the Côte des Blancs. The approach to vineyard management is bio-dynamic at every stage.

items.name: Cristal Rosé

notes.taste: Salmon pink hue with golden tints. It reveals a lively palate invigorated by an incredibly elegant effervescence and beautiful light bubbles that soften the fruity texture. The nose exudes delicate, zesty, fresh and precise notes of citrus peel, forest fruit, mandarin, raspberry and wild strawberry.
notes.food: This is fantastic with lobster, caviar, gourmet salad and foie gras. It also works with seared salmon and poached sea trout.
notes.made: A blend of 56% Pinot Noir and 44% Chardonnay, comprising 15% of wine vinified in wood (oak tuns), which undergoes weekly bâtonnage (stirring by hand); it is not subjected to malolactic fermentation. The Cristal Rosé cuvée is aged, on average, for six years in Roederer’s cellars and left for eight months after dégorgement (disgorging) to attain the perfect balance. The wine making technique called 'infusion' is used where a small amount of Chardonnay juice is added to the Pinot noir maceration which then ferment together and integrate smoothly and harmoniously..
notes.vines: The first Vintage was made in 1974. The selected old-vine Pinot noir grapes are from the finest Grand Cru vineyards at Aÿ, which are now cultivated according to biodynamic principles. The unique calcareous clay soil, which gives the grapes an exquisite minerality, enables the vines (made in only the best years) to attain exceptional fruit maturity, complemented by a crystalline acidity.

items.name: Rosé Vintage

notes.taste: There is a complex bouquet of subtle minty freshness combined with zesty fruit, wild strawberry and raspberry. The nose opens out to reveal spicy and smoky notes, characteristic of the Pinot Noirs grown in Cumières, along with the aromas of dried fruit, roasted almonds and cocoa beans. There are underlying saline notes, reminiscent of sea spray.
notes.food: A fantastic pairing with fish such as salmon and tuna; meat including lamb, veal, pheasant and soft cheeses such. It can also be served with red fruit based deserts that are less sweet.
notes.made: Louis Roederer developed a unique technique for the production of its rosé champagnes. This process is referred to as the ‘infusion’ technique (a small amount of Chardonnay juice is added to the Pinot Noir maceration which then ferments together to integrate harmoniously). Vinified approximately 25% in old oak casks and bottle-aged 4 years before being left to rest for a further 6 months after disgorging in order to attain perfect maturity.
notes.vines: The Pinot Noir is from the Champagne crus village of Cumières, for which the steeply-sloping, shallow clay and limestone soils face south and benefit from additional light reflected from the river Marne, enabling great phenolic maturity to be achieved. The Chardonnay is from the north facing slopes in Chouilly, bringing bright and fresh notes.

notes.taste: The fruity aromas of wild red berries are followed by floral notes, scents of zest, sweet and spicy, while the nuances of dried fruits and then cocoa evoke aging in oak wood. Rich, fleshy, the Brut Rosé exalts the maturity of the fruit. With its shimmering effervescence and its first impression of freshness, it opens with smoothness on almost exotic notes, mixed with the pure minerality of Chardonnays.
notes.food: Great with salmon, lamb and even pheasant. Also goes very well with creamy cheeses. For dessert, serve it with a sabayon.
notes.made: 17% of the wines are vinified in wood (oak barrels) with weekly stirring. 30% malolactic fermentation. To make rosé champagnes, the bleeding method is used after cold skin maceration. The Brut Rosé cuvée benefits from an average of 4 years of maturation in the cellars and also a rest of 6 months after disgorging in order to perfect its maturity. The dosage is adapted to each vintage between 8 and 10 g/l.

In these selected terroirs, Louis Roederer applies precision viticulture adapted to the production of a saignée rosé.

items.name: Campofiorin

notes.taste: Intense ruby red with aromas of ripe cherries and sweet spices. Sumptuous and rich, intense berry fruit; soft tannins with lingering flavours.
notes.food: An exceptionally versatile wine. Good with pasta dishes dressed with rich sauces (meat or mushrooms). Also a great accompaniment for grilled and roasted meat. Ideal with well-aged cheese.
notes.made: Made with Masi's double fermentation method where the wine from the fresh grapes are re-fermented with 25% of the whole semi-dried grapes (dried for about six weeks) of the same varieties. This fermentation lasts for about 15 days at 18-20°C. The malolactic fermentation takes place immediately afterwards. The process enriches the wine in colour and alcohol while extracting elegant tannins, which brings additional new flavours and aromas. The wine is matured for a minimum18 months in wood, 2/3 in Slavonian oak barrels of 90 hl, 1/3 in Allier and Slavonian new barrels of 600 liters, and a minimum of 3 months of bottle ageing.
notes.vines: Vineyards in the stream-filled valleys of the Veronese hills which enjoy similar climatic conditions to the original “Campofiorin” vineyard in Marano di Valpolicella. Very deep alluvial terrain with limestone soil.

items.name: Costasera Amarone
items.designation: Denominazione di origine controllata e garantita (DOCG)

notes.taste: Deep ruby red with brilliant reflections. Intense and elegant aromas of cherry and plum jam with spicy hints of cinnamon and cloves. Firm structure but very soft on the palate with velvety tannins and a marked acidity that balances the alcohol level well. Attractively long and full flavoured with a fruity finish and soft spiciness.
notes.food: Amarone is a full-bodied wine for grilled or roasted red meats, game, and strong tasty cheeses, such as parmesan. Famous as a “meditation” wine, it is a great after-dinner drink. Recommended drinking temperature is 20°C (68° F).
notes.made: Amarone is the product of a wine-making method the Ancient Romans called "appassimento" which involved grape drying. At the end of September or the beginning of October, the best clusters of grapes from hillside vineyards are picked and laid out on bamboo racks in special lofts. By the end of January the grapes have lost 35% of their original weight and have highly concentrated sugars. Only the Corvina grapes are naturally attacked by noble rot. The processes that follow are: soft pressing; partial destalking; 45 days fermentation in large Slavonian oak barrels or stainless steel vats at low, natural temperatures; transfer into barrels of 30-40 hl where the alcoholic fermentation continues for 35 days in the presence of selected alcohol resistant yeasts; and malolactic fermentation. 28-30 months with 80% aged in Slavonian oak barrels of 40-80 hl and 20% in small Allier and Slavonian oak barrels (40% new, 30% second usage, 30% third usage). The wine is then bottle-aged for a minimum of 4 months.
notes.vines: From Masi’s hillside vineyards on west and south-west facing slopes in the historic Valpolicella Classico communes of Marano, Negrar, S.Ambrogio and San Pietro in Cariano. The soil is red limestone with cretaceous marl.

items.name: Costasera Riserva Amarone
items.designation: Denominazione di origine controllata e garantita (DOCG)

notes.taste: Thick, deep, ruby red in colour. Elegant and intense aromas of ripe berry fruit, accompanied by delicate hints of cocoa and cinnamon. Firm and full bodied structure on the palate, with silky tannins, smooth alcohol and a refreshing acidity to give balance and measure. Very long on the finish with tastes of marasca cherries and cinnamon.
notes.food: A majestic, complex and elegant wine. It has great ageing potential. Good with red meat, game and mature cheeses. Excellent finale to a meal. Serve at 18°C.
notes.made: Amarone is made using the ancient '"appassimento" (partial grape drying) method in use since Roman times. At the end of September/beginning of October the best bunches from the hillside vineyards are picked and laid out on traditional bamboo racks (“arele”) in special lofts where the natural drying process is controlled by the NASA system. By the middle of February the grapes have lost about 40% of their weight and have acquired great concentration. Of the grapes used, only the Corvina grape is subject to a slight natural attack of "botrytis" (noble rot). The Oseleta grapes confer greater tannic structure and deeper colour to the wine after drying. The grapes are pressed gently after partial destalking and fermented for 45 days in large Slavonian oak barrels or in stainless steel vats at ambient cellar temperatures. The final fermentation takes 35 days in 30-40 hectolitre barrels, induced by the inoculation of selected yeasts highly resistant to alcohol and the malolactic fermentation. 38-40 months in 600-litre Slavonian and Allier oak casks (1/3 new, 1/3 2nd passage, 1/3 3rd passage). Six months bottle ageing minimum.
notes.vines: Hillside vineyards belonging to Masi on slopes facing the sunset (west/southwest) in historic Amarone production locations of the Valpolicella Classico area (the communes of Marano, Negrar, Sant' Ambrogio and San Pietro in Cariano). Loose red soil on Eocene limestone and tight packed red soil on basalt.

items.name: Masianco
items.designation: DOP/DOC Denominazione di orgine controllata / protetta

notes.taste: Deep straw yellow in colour with golden reflections. The nose stands out with finesse and elegance, showing a lovely bouquet of ripe fruit and delicate aromas of honey and vanilla. Soft and refreshing at the same time on the palate thanks to the lively acidity coming from the Pinot Grigio and the body and structure coming from the light appassimento given to the Verduzzo. A long and dry finish.
notes.food: Masianco is an ideal aperitif. Perfect with hors d’oeuvres, fish, and white meats. A medium bodied white wine with great personality, ideal for modern cuisine in general. Recommended serving temperature is between 8-10° C (46-50° F).
notes.made: The two grape varieties are harvested and vinified separately. The Pinot Grigio grapes are picked at the end of August and vinified immediately (for 25 days, from 15° to 10°C) in order to enhance freshness and bouquet. The Verduzzo grapes are harvested at the end of September, then further ripened on racks for three weeks in a process "Appassimento" particularly suitable to this varietal because of its thick skin; the result is a better concentration of fruit. After a short criomaceration (36 hours at 5°C) the Verduzzo starts its fermentation in stainless steel tanks and is then transferred to barriques where it also completes the malolactic. 3 months: stainless steel tanks for the Pinot Grigio, barriques for the Verduzzo. The wine is then assembled before 45 days bottle ageing.
notes.vines: From the “Stra’ del Milione” vineyards at Castions di Strada, Friuli. Soil conditions are mainly calcareous sediments on basalt and clay soil.

notes.food: A great aperitif that goes well with seafood, vegetarian dishes and with fresh cheeses.
notes.made: From the region of Friuli-Venezia Giulia. The main grape training system used is the Guyot and Sylvoz.

items.name: Toar Valpolicella
items.designation: DOP/DOC Denominazione di orgine controllata / protetta

notes.taste: Intense, dark, ruby red colour with violet reflections. Attractive red fruit aromas, including marasca cherries, on the nose, plus spices such as cocoa and licorice. Firm but well integrated tannins on the palate, plus vibrant acidity and juicy tastes of ripe fruit and spices. Long and intense on the finish.
notes.food: This full-bodied red wine goes well with grilled or roasted meat, roast beef, game, and moderately matured cheeses. Recommended drinking temperature is 18° C (64° F).
notes.made: The three grape varieties are picked when they are fully ripe. The Corvina and Rondinella are vinified together, the Oseleta is vinified separately. De-stalking is followed by fermentation with selected yeasts and 20 days’maceration at temperatures between 20-24°C. The malolactic fermentation follows. 14 months: French oak barrels (50% new, 50% II passage) and Slavonian barrels (50% new, 50% II passage) for the wine made from Corvina and Rondinella; new oak barriques (50% French, 50% Slavonian) for the wine made from Oseleta. 5 months in bottle after the assemblage.
notes.vines: Selected areas in the hills between the valleys of Negrar and Marano in Valpolicella, usually employed for the production of Amarone. West-South-West exposure. Volcanic soil and, specifically, outcrops of volcanic tufo known locally as “toar”. The rich concentration of minerals in the soil gives the wine a special intensity of aroma and structure.

items.name: Valpolicella Bonacosta
items.designation: DOP/DOC Denominazione di orgine controllata / protetta

notes.taste: A bright red wine with purple tinges. Full bouquet with aromas reminiscent of cherries and green pepper. Smooth on the palate with delicate tannins and good acidity to give excellent freshness of taste. The flavours end with a long, fruity finish.
notes.food: A versatile wine enough to go with many dishes. Perfect with soups, pasta and risottos. Very good with both simple and more substantial dishes based on red meat, or with fresh cheeses. Recommended drinking temperature 18° C (64° F).
notes.made: The grapes are harvested separately (mid September for Molinara and Rondinella, end of September for Corvina). Fermentation at controlled temperatures (25-28°C) using selected yeasts. Contact with the skins lasts 16 days for Corvina, 10 days for the other grapes. Fermentation lasts 20 days in total and is followed by complete malolactic fermentation. It is further matured for 4 months in 60-90 hl. Slavonian oak barrels. 20% of the Corvina is aged in new Allier and Slavonian small oak casks.
notes.vines: The grapes are sourced from the Masi vineyards in the hills of the historic Valpolicella Classico zone. The soil is predominately red calcareous sediments on basalt. The historic production areas such as Valpolicella Classica and the higher morainic hillside area of Bardolino are good for both quality and quantity.

items.name: Canevel Setage Valdobbiandene Brut
items.designation: Denominazione di origine controllata e garantita (DOCG)

notes.taste: Pale straw in colour, bright and lively with abundant froth and a fine, elegant perlage. Golden delicious apple and spiced aromas. Dry, soft yet characterful.
notes.food: The favorite aperitif on all occasions, to be sipped with fresh summer appetizers, vegetable crudités, sushi, oysters, and fish tartare.
notes.made: A benchmark in the Canevel range: a dry and silky sparkling wine with delicate aromas of Golden delicious apples and spices. Canevel sparkling wines are characterized by subtle, elegant bubbles like silk, thanks to the original process called "Setàge" (the term comes from ‘seta’, the Italian for silk).
notes.vines: Situated on a hill and surrounded by rows of Glera vines, the grape variety used for Treviso Prosecco, Canevel is a ‘château’ property in the historic heart of the Prosecco producing area, Valdobbiadene DOCG. From the outset, we chose to integrate the entire production line, from selection and care of the vineyards to vinification and sparkling wine making, controlling the entire production process, to guarantee the highest quality.

items.name: Pian del Griso Pinot Grigio
items.designation: DOP/DOC Denominazione di orgine controllata / protetta

notes.taste: Bright straw yellow in colour. Elegant, refined, floral and fruity aromas on the nose with hints of apples and pears and a slight touch of minerality. Good supporting acidity to give balance to soft structure, giving perfect harmony of taste. Long and attractive on the finish, which ends with the same fruitiness and minerality first seen on the nose.
notes.food: An excellent aperitif. it goes very good with antipasti, soups, fish and white meats. Serve at 10°C (50°F).
notes.made: Whole grape pressing, fermentation in stainless steel at 14-15°C for about 20 days with the use of selected yeasts. The wine rests on the lees for about 4-5 months with regular batonnage and an additional 15 days in bottle.
notes.vines: The vineyards are on the Fojaneghe estate in the communes of Mori and Isera (Trentino) at a height of 300 metres above-sea-level. The ground is typically layered sedimentary moraine. Breezes from Lake Garda bring good temperature variations from night to day and excellent general ventilation.

notes.taste: Bright straw yellow with greenish reflections. Typical Sauvignon Blanc aromas on the nose, accompanied by a bouquet of fresh fruit. Good supporting acidity on the palate: long lasting and well integrated with a long, dry finish.
notes.food: Perfect as an aperitif. Recommended also with starters, light summer dishes, fish, pizza, cold cuts and poultry. Recommended drinking temperature 10-12° C (50-56° F).
notes.made: The Garganega and Sauvignon Blanc grapes are harvested and vinified separately in temperature-controlled stainless steel tanks (12-16°C). Selected yeasts are used for this process. The Sauvignon is off-skin vinified for 15-18 days, but the Garganega has about 12 hours on-skin contact before a fermentation which lasts about 20-22 days. The Sauvignon finishes its fermentation in barriques, where it then remains for 2 months before being blended with the tank-fermented Garganega.
notes.vines: Sourced from the Serego Alighieri vineyards in Gargagnago di Sant’Ambrogio di Valpolicella. The soil is composed of compact red sediment, with sufficient humus, over Eocenic limestone. The peculiarities of this kind of alluvial soil, together with a microclimate which is influenced by the cool temperatures of the basin of the river Adige, make for ideal growing conditions for the production of white wines.

items.name: Possessioni Valpolicella
items.designation: DOP/DOC Denominazione di orgine controllata / protetta

notes.taste: Bright ruby red in colour with slight purple overtones. Berry fruit and plums on the nose with spiciness provided by hints of cloves and black peppercorns. Good balance between the acidity that delivers freshness on the palate and well integrated tannins. A long fruit-filled finish.
notes.food: A versatile wine that can be served throughout a meal. Perfect with red meats and lightly matured cheeses. Best served at 18°C (68° F).
notes.made: Fermentation lasts about 15 days at a temperature of 24-26°C in a process designed to make an expressive wine with a great bouquet. The stainless steel tanks are then closed and maceration continues for a further 10 days. The wine is then matured in barrels, where it undergoes malolactic fermentation. During the following months the wine is subject to batonnage every other day. It is then matured 8 to 9 months in Slavonian oak barrels of 25 hl; 3 months in cherry wood casks of 600 l; minimum 3 months bottle ageing.
notes.vines: Corvina, Rondinella, Molinara (Serego Alighieri clone). Grapres are soureced from the Serego Alighieri vineyards in Gargagnago di Sant’Ambrogio di Valpolicella. The soil is compact red sediment, over eocenic limestone. Excellent exposure for producing wines of great quality.

items.name: Vaio Amaron
items.designation: Denominazione di origine controllata e garantita (DOCG)

notes.taste: The wine is deep ruby red, almost impenetrable. Elegant intensity of aromas: berry fruit preserved in spirit, dried plums and cocoa. Intense and well balanced on the palate: full bodied with silky tannins and a firm structure. It ends with a long finish of ripe cherries and sweet spices.
notes.food: Ideal with red meats, game, quail, roasts, and other richly-flavoured dishes. Excellent paired with strong cheeses (such as parmesan, pecorino etc.). A noble after-dinner wine. Recommended drinking temperature 18° C (64° F).
notes.made: Amarone is the product of the ancient wine making method called "appassimento" (grape drying). At the end of September or beginning of October the best bunches are laid on bamboo racks in the old lofts of estate buildings where large windows provide natural ventilation. By the middle of February the grapes weigh 35-40% less. Only the Corvina grape is affected by botrytis ("noble rot"). After a delicate pressing, the dried grapes, which are partially destalked, ferment for 48 days in large Slavonian oak barrels, at low, natural temperatures (the weather is very cold at this time of year); then the wine continues to ferment until the sugar has been totally transformed into alcohol and the malolactic fermentation takes place. The wine is then matured for 3 years in Slavonian oak barrels of 6-20 hl, 4 months in cherry wood casks, then a minimum of 5 months in the bottle.
notes.vines: The Vaio Armaron vineyard, in Gargagnago (commune of Sant'Ambrogio di Valpolicella); property of the conti Serego Alighieri family. Altitude 230-265 metres a.s.l., vineyards face south-west. Red terrain, rich in humus, on limestone and clay, good drainage. Terraces supported by dry stone walls (“marogne”). The particular terrain and climatic conditions permit only limited production, but of very high quality.

items.name: Il Bianco di Ludovico
items.designation: DOP/DOC Denominazione di orgine controllata / protetta

notes.taste: Our Pinot Noir opens with juicy red-fleshed Black Doris plum accented by notes of wild berries. Spice characters follow through on the palate with warm, soft tannins and a velvety texture.
notes.made: With every step of the winemaking process our goal is to preserve the incredible aromatics and scintillating structure of our wines. After harvesting, we keep the fruit as cool as possible to retain bright, fresh Marlborough fruit flavours. Gentle crushing helps to preserve the personality of the variety and the influence of the site. We use traditional punch downs during fermentation to extract optimum colour and soft tannins. Our Pinot Noir is aged in French oak barriques to add complexity. 9 months in French oak (15% new barrels)
notes.vines: The winding Dashwood Pass connects Marlborough’s two marquee winegrowing regions, the Awatere and Wairau Valleys. Since 1989, Dashwood wines have been crafted by blending fruit sourced from these neighbouring yet distinct coastal terroirs. Our wines are true reflections of the Marlborough region: as cool as the winds in our valleys, and as imposing as the mountains that frame our vineyards. The Floral symbol on our wine labels is the pohutukawa, a maori word meaning drenched with mist. it is an evergreen tree known as the unoffIcial new zealand christmas tree due to its bright red blooms that emerge every december.

items.name: The Ned Sauvignon Blanc

notes.taste: Ripe aromas of gooseberry and white peach are laced with refreshing notes of lime. The fleshy mid palate is tamed by an underlying minerally acid backbone that culminates in a bright, zesty finish.
notes.food: An amazing match with scallops sautéed in garlic butter along with a crunchy green garden salad. These delicate flavours will complement the bright varietal characters of this wine.
notes.made: 100% Sauvignon Blanc which is field destemmed before being gently pressed into stainless steel tanks. The juice is fermented at cool temperatures with selected yeast strains aimed at developing a full flavour spectrum; from green and citrus notes to riper, more tropical flavours.
notes.vines: Within the Marlborough wine region, Waihopai River Vineyard lies on the flats on the right bank of the Waihopai River, at the mouth of the Waihopai Valley. By far the most substantial part of the 260ha vineyard is planted in Sauvignon Blanc. What makes the Waihopai River Vineyard such a great place is the exceptional diversity across the one site. It consists of three terraces, formed by glacial movement over thousands of years. The bottom terrace consists of the old river bed, with silt, silty clay loam and gravel soils. Diverging seams of varying soils give real diversity of flavours to work with. The middle terrace has more gutsy soil, with more fertile topsoil overlaying the gravels below. This area also gives a wide range of flavours and characteristics. The top terrace is the largest of the three, and varies across its width from west to east. The soils from the west of the terrace are very similar to the mid-terrace, and as you go towards the Delta Hill, the soils get gradually deeper and richer, and in this area specifically, the shade that the hill provides adds to the variable conditions.

The final blend was made further to tests and analysis conducted during this period. To preserve the highest possible quality, the wine was only subject to light fining and filtration prior to bottling.
notes.vines: The grapes were sourced from the Douro Superior sub-region, namely from Quinta da Leda and from winegrowers with their own vineyards, preferably exposed to the North and at a higher altitude.

notes.taste: A beautiful red colour, with intense tawny shades that recall its slow maturation in wood. Its bouquet is intense and rich with hints of very ripe fruit (plum, apricot and marmalade) and floral notes. Complex, its spice and nutty notes derive from the evolution in oak wood, through oxidation In the mouth, it is a full-bodied and rich-flavoured wine, extremely well balanced, that combines elegance with a delicate yet persistent finish.
notes.food: It is very good served on its own, accompanying some selected entrées or as a dessert wine. It also beautiful with most sweets, desserts and cheeses. Serve slightly cold for fuller appreciation.
notes.made: Sourced grapes are vinified using the traditional Porto Wine method. Hand-picked grapes are softly crushed and, after partial stalk-removal, fermented with maceration allowing the best components of the grape skins to be extracted. The whole process takes place under strict control of both temperature and wine density, making it possible for the winemaker to choose the ideal moment for the addition of wine alcohol, fundamental to halt fermentation and keep Porto wine natural sweetness. The wines selected for the final blend of this reserve Porto wine stay in the Douro after the harvest and are taken to the company´s traditional Porto Wine lodges in V.N.Gaia the following Spring where they mature in oak casks. For several years the wines undergo numerous transfers, analyses and tasting that monitor the ageing of wines, preparation of blends, as well as refreshing and eventual adjustment when tasting so determines. The final blend is composed with wines from different ages and origins to achieve a consistency of style and quality typical of Porto Ferreira Dona Antónia Reserva Tawny. The selected wines usually varies between 4 and 12 years of age, achieving an average age of about 7 years. Tawny ports are wines usually made from red grapes that are aged in wooden barrels exposing them to gradual oxidation and evaporation. As a result of this oxidation, they mellow to a golden-brown colour.
notes.vines: A premium reserve red Porto Wine, created to celebrate the memory of the charismatic lady - Dona Antónia Adelaide Ferreira - that in the 19th century led and inspired the company to gain its future, confirming the values that would established it as leading quality producer and number one brand in Portugal. This port is a blend of grapes from Douro Valley: Tinta Amarela; Tinta Barroca; Tinta Cão; Tinta Roriz; Touriga Franca; Touriga Nacional.

items.house: The House of Ferreirinha, was founded in the eighteenth century by Bernardo Ferreira, whose company philosophy was carried on, especially by his granddaughter Dona Antonia Ferreira, known affectionately as ‘Ferreirinha’. The company was acquired by Sogrape in 1987 and the Ferreira core values were past on to present day which continue to be very crucial to the quality of products while remaining true to their proud heritage.

items.name: 7 Years Gran Reserva

notes.taste: An intense red shading to tawny at the rim. A range of different characteristics can be identified on the nose – black cherry fruit, balsamic, leather, tobacco and vanilla oak. Medium to full bodied with real finesse, concentrated red fruit flavours, mellow tannins and a smooth finish.
notes.food: Great with game, roast beef and other grilled red meats, rich vegetarian dishes and mature cheeses.
notes.made: 100 %Tempranillo grapes were hand picked from 30 year-old vines in stony vineyards. Fermentation was at controlled temperatures (25-28º C) in stainless steel tanks for 8-10 days. The wine was then matured for at least eighteen months in oak barriques with varying toasting levels.
notes.vines: Sourced from the winery, Bodegas Navalón in Valdepeñas which means “valley of stones” – in late August/early September. The soils are clayey lime and there is a chalky layer which retains water to refresh the vines. Altitude helps moderate summer heat, as the climate in Valdepeñas is classic continental, with cold winters and long hot, dry summers.

items.house: After extensive tasting of the best cuvées available in the cellars of Bodegas Navalón, Master of Wine Norrel Robertson selects the wine for Anciano. Bodegas Navalón is amidst the ancient vineyards of DO Valdepeñas. It is a family owned winery, part of a company that was originally founded at the start of the 20th Century by Don Juan Sánchez. Grapes are sourced from small growers to make the classic red wine which is aged in oak barrel.

items.name: 10 Year Old

notes.taste: Sweet green apple and pear complement creamy dark honey. Soft vanilla develops alongside gentle smoke. Smooth flavours of malted cereal and stewed fruit combine with warm toffee and a hint of black cherry. Full bodied finish with malted cereal persevering and lingering soft smoke. 92 Points, Whisky Advocate "This expression was distilled from malt peated to 12 to 14 ppm, and aged in 80% bourbon and 20% sherry casks before a final year in more sherry casks. Sweet smoke on the early nose, with malt, vanilla, quite dry sherry, apple, and toffee. Smoky barley, vanilla, subtle sherry, and light honey on the palate. Peaches, ginger, and woodsmoke on the medium-length finish. Very accomplished. ” 91 Points, Wine Enthusiast "This copper-hued whiskey offers concentrated caramel, pecan pie and oak aromas. The palate is oaky and drying, not as luscious as the aroma suggests, showing vanilla and spice, plus hints of baked apple and cocoa. Adding water brings out more nutty flavor and a whiff of smoke.”
notes.made: We are a traditional Speyside distillery owned by a family of whisky-lovers intent on making single malt the right way with true character. Only ever matured in the finest oak casks, our signature TEN YEARS OLD single malt delivers delicate forest fruits and creamy malt, a touch of smoke and rich, lasting sherry notes.
notes.vines: 43% vol First fill bourbon and sherry casks

items.house: Benromach Distillery was established in Forres, Scotland in 1898. It was the realisation of a long-held dream for the Urquhart family when they acquired the distillery in 1993. Five years of meticulous refitting of the distillery followed before officially reopening our doors in 1998. Our whisky is handcrafted and reminiscent of a time when Speyside distilleries malted their own barley using peat to fuel the fires and impart a touch of smoke.

items.name: 40 Year Old

notes.taste: Matured in the finest hand-selected first-fill Oloroso sherry casks, our FORTY YEAR OLD single malt delivers rich ginger and stewed fruit aromas. Seville orange, red apple and demerara sugar followed by a citrus zest finish.
notes.made: Benromach Distillery in Speyside has unveiled the first annual batch release of its 40 Years Old, with just over 1,000 bottles available worldwide. Bottled at a cask strength of 57.1%, this rare single malt whisky is natural in colour and was laid down in 1981 before spending four decades maturing in the finest first-fill Oloroso sherry casks. The result is an exquisite single malt and the oldest expression released by Benromach.
notes.vines: Benromach is a traditional Speyside distillery owned by a family intent on producing single malt using time honoured methods. Its small team of distillers rely entirely on their expertise and senses to make the finest handmade whisky. A small number of casks maturing in its dunnage warehouses were selected for this first annual batch release, with a further release planned each year.

items.name: 12 Year Old

notes.taste: Butterscotch and honey playing the lead, with raisins and mocha in the background. 90 Points, IWSC 2019 "Aromatic and perfumed, with vanilla, bananas and coconuts on the first impression. Sweet and lifted on the palate, with a light and creamy mouthfeel. This is an easy-drinking example, with a charming bourbon vanilla finish.” Ralfy's Whisky of the Year 2019. Double Gold, San Francisco Spirits Competition 2020
notes.food: "World's Best Single Malt" - World Whisky Awards 2025
notes.made: In this era of mergers and consolidations we go against the grain; an independent, Scottish owned and managed whisky company. We chose to step away from the corporate treadmill and short-term targets. Instead, we focus on the important things; making great whisky and enjoying life. It is in this tradition that we would like to introduce the most important release in the history of The GlenAllachie Distillers Company; GlenAllachie 12 year old, the heart of our range, a landmark bottling. Our best casks selected and bottled under the careful eye of our Master Distiller Billy Walker.
notes.vines: The GlenAllachie 12 Year Old is bottled at 46%, non chill filtered and natural colour.

items.house: One of Scotland’s few independently owned and managed distilleries, The GlenAllachie is led by industry veteran, Billy Walker, who boasts an almost 50-year tenure in whisky. Nestled at the foot of Ben Rinnes, the distillery lies at the heart of the Speyside, with a focus upon quality over quantity. Spanning 16 on-site warehouses, our passionate team have complete control, giving them the freedom to make decisions for all the right reasons.

notes.taste: The comforting aroma of baked goodness, jammy ripe fruit with walnuts and orange honey come in first. A rich honey sweetness emerges, accompanied by hints of black tea spice and dried fruits. Richness of toasted cereal grain rounded out by honeysuckle notes. An energetic lingering, smooth finish of perfectly balanced warm spice.
notes.food: Find some recipes such as the Mystic Charmer, Bond Fire and Bourbon Sunset at https://brothersbondbourbon.com/our-recipes/
notes.made: "Brother’s Bond is a story of time and quality; two things we all cherish in life. Our friendship’s true bond strengthened while drinking bourbon, both on and off-screen for over a decade. Brother’s Bond is a nod to our on-screen characters, our shared love for great bourbon, and a reflection of the brotherhood we have formed over the years.” - Ian Somerhalder and Paul Wesley
notes.vines: A four-grain, high-rye straight bourbon whiskey with a mash bill of 65% corn, 22% rye, wheat and barley making up the rest. The copper column and copper pot-doubler distillation method creates a spirit full of flavor and texture. Then the spirit is aged for a minimum of 4 years in virgin American oak barrels with a deep char #4 on the staves and # 2 char on the barrel heads.

notes.taste: Classic from the get-go. Black cassis, pipe tobacco, and black cherry saturates the mouth. Followed by forest floor, dark plum, and pencil lead. Great density and a tremendous finesse-filled finish which one has to repeat...A CLASSIC!
notes.made: Wines of Substance was conceived by winemaker Charles Smith with a single-minded vision: to produce the best value-priced varietal wines in America. Substance is made with traditional winemaking techniques: natural fermentations, barrel-aging and bottled unfiltered and unfined. In essence, Charles makes Substance wines with small batch winemaking integrity on an unprecedented scale.
notes.vines: 100% Cabernet Sauvignon from Columbia Valley Vineyard(s): Goose Ridge, Painted Hills, Badger Mountain, Shaw, Sportsfisher, Coyote Production: 4.5 tons per acre | Native yeast | 100% whole berry fermentation | 41 days on skins | 50% new French oak barriques | 11 months barrel-aged on lees

items.name: Morning Fog Chardonnay

notes.taste: Aromatics burst of citrus, lemon, pear and toasty oak. This wine is balanced by hints of vanilla and citrus on the palate, finishing with a nice acidity.
notes.food: Grilled shrimp tacos, pasta primavera and grilled corn.
notes.made: This wine is composed from a blend of Chardonnay (98 %) and Gewurztraminer (2 %). 50% barrel fermented in neutral American oak barrels and 50% fermented in stainless steel tanks. Bâtonnage, the art of stirring the barrels, was performed monthly. A portion was Barrel fermented and aged sur lie (on the lees) for 5 months. A portion in stainless steel was half aged on the lees for 5 months while the other half was racked clean to preserve the fresh fruit characters.
notes.vines: The estate grown Chardonnay is named for the morning coastal fog pushed by Pacific wind streams into the bowl of the San Francisco Bay, and lured inland by Livermore Valley’s unique East-West orientation. This daily phenomenon moderates the climate to produce excellent, beautifully balanced Chardonnay. Planted on various Wente clones, which are all harvested and vinified separately, the variation within the vineyards adds to the complexity of the wine.

items.house: Founded 137 years ago, Wente Vineyards is the oldest, continuously operated family-owned winery in the United States. Located in the historic Livermore Valley, Wente Vineyards is recognized as one of California’s premier wine country destinations, featuring wine tasting, food and wine pairing, events and championship golf.

items.name: Southern Hills Cabernet Sauvignon

notes.taste: The bouquet has welcoming aromatics of warm baking spices. On the palate this wine delivers ripe blackberry and fig with round, smooth tannins.
notes.food: Pairs very well with grilled cheese, tomato soup and a club sandwich.
notes.made: The wine is a blend of Cabernet Sauvignon (78 %), Petite Sirah (19 %) and Petite Verdot (3 %); percentages slightly differ from each vintage. Wine was pressed on the skins after 7-12 days. Varietals were fermented separately in upright stainless steel fermenters and pumped over twice daily. Aged for 16 months in a combination of French, American and neutral oak barrels as well as stainless steel tanks to add fruit vibrancy.
notes.vines: Livermore Valley’s unique East-West orientation, well-drained rocky soils, and unique mesoclimates, the Southern Hills vineyards are located in the most desirable settings with exposures ideal for growing Cabernet Sauvignon of distinct character, depth and intensity. The Estate Grown Southern Hills Cabernet Sauvignon is named for our vineyards located along the southern hills of the Livermore Valley. The Wente family farms approximately 400 acres of Cabernet Sauvignon vineyards using the two clones originating from California wine pioneer Charles Wetmore’s Bordeaux cuttings in the 19th century.
